title: From busy to progress: KPIs, baselines and SMART targets

say: From busy to progress: KPIs, baselines and SMART targets.
This is the video for module 1 of Reporting and Performance Tracking.

Many hardworking women end the month tired, but unsure whether the business actually moved forward. Performance tracking means writing down a few chosen numbers on a regular schedule, so you can answer with evidence instead of feelings.
Inputs are what you put in: money, flour, data bundles, your hours.
Activities are what you do: baking, posting adverts, holding a training.
Outputs are what you produce and can count straight away, like 250 snack packs.
Outcomes are the changes that matter, like 220 packs sold and 29,000 naira profit.
A report that says we held 12 meetings tells nothing about whether they worked. Good tracking always includes at least one outcome.
For example, Bisi sells meat pies in Ibadan. In week 1 she posted 30 status updates, got 12 orders and collected 54,000 naira. That is 1,800 naira per post.

panel.heading: Bisi's busy week and good week

say: In week 2 she was ill and posted only 15 times, yet got 14 orders and 63,000 naira. That is 4,200 naira per post.
Her week 2 posts had clear photos and prices. The type of post mattered more than the number. Without writing it down, she would have kept working harder on the wrong thing.

panel.heading: Bisi's busy week and good week

say: A KPI, or key performance indicator, is one of the few numbers you choose because it best shows whether you are reaching your goal. If everything is a KPI, nothing is.

panel.heading: Five checks for a good KPI
items: Measurable with data you can get

say: Check that each one is linked to your goal, clearly defined, measurable with data you can actually get, something you can influence, and few in number.
Watch out for vanity metrics like likes and views. They feel good, but often do not lead to money or change.

panel.heading: Five checks for a good KPI
items: Measurable with data you can get

say: Ratios make different weeks fair to compare. In March, Bisi had 80 price enquiries and 20 paid orders. Her conversion rate is 25%. One in four people who asked a price ended up buying.

cards.d: 20 orders from 80 enquiries. 20 divided by 80 is 25%. One in four buyers.
90,000 naira of sales from 20 orders is 4,500 naira per order.
7 of her 20 orders came from past buyers. That is 35%.

say: Her total sales were 90,000 naira, so her average order value is 4,500 naira.

say: 7 orders came from people who had bought before. Her repeat customer rate is 35%.
She mixes lagging indicators, like monthly sales, with leading ones, like weekly enquiries, which warn her early.

say: A baseline is where you are now, measured before you try to improve. Use at least four weeks of records, because one week can be unusual.
Bisi's four weeks add up to 240,000 naira.
Divided by 4, her baseline is 60,000 naira a week.
She plans one new action, a Saturday delivery slot, and chooses a 15% increase. 60,000 times 1.15 is 69,000 naira.
Her SMART target is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound: raise average weekly sales from 60,000 to 69,000 naira for the four weeks ending 31 March.
Tracking often means writing down details about real people. Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023 sets rules for this. Collect only what you need.

say: To remember. Effort is not the result. Choose 3 to 5 KPIs. Use ratios to compare fairly. Measure a baseline before you set a target.
And progress is actual divided by target, times 100. If Bisi averages 64,000 naira, that is about 93% of her target.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Activity shows effort; outcomes show results
Choose 3 to 5 KPIs that pass the five checks
Ratios make weeks fair to compare
Baseline first, then a SMART target
Progress = actual divided by target x 100

say: Now practise. Map the results chain for your own work, and write one tracking question. Draft three to five KPIs, each with a definition and data source. Then calculate a baseline and write one SMART target, and check your 2-Step Verification is on.
